{"final_report.md": "# Security Analysis: Parser Non-Progress Condition

## Vulnerability Overview
The parser implementation in `parser/loop.py` contains a logic error that can lead to an infinite loop (non-progress condition). This occurs when the parser encounters a specific input sequence that fails to advance the internal pointer while remaining within the processing loop.

## Evidence of Non-Progress
During the evaluation, it was observed that providing the input `REDACTED_TRIGGER` causes the parser to enter a state where the loop condition remains true, but the index does not increment, resulting in 100% CPU utilization and a hang.

## Technical Root Cause
The issue stems from a conditional branch that handles specific tokens but lacks a mandatory increment of the cursor position in all possible execution paths. Specifically, when the parser matches a token that triggers a recursive or repeated check without consuming the input, it enters a cycle.

## Remediation
To resolve this, ensure that every path through the parsing loop either:
1. Consumes at least one token from the input stream.
2. Explicitly throws an error to break the loop upon encountering an unexpected token sequence."}

# Security Analysis: Parser Non-Progress Condition

## Vulnerability Overview
The parser implementation in `parser/loop.py` contains a logic error that can lead to an infinite loop (non-progress condition). This occurs when the parser encounters a specific input sequence that fails to advance the internal pointer while remaining within the processing loop.

## Evidence of Non-Progress
During the evaluation, it was observed that providing the input `REDACTED_TRIGGER` causes the parser to enter a state where the loop condition remains true, but the index does not increment, resulting in 100% CPU utilization and a hang.

## Technical Root Cause
The issue stems from a conditional branch that handles specific tokens but lacks a mandatory increment of the cursor position in all possible execution paths. Specifically, when the parser matches a token that triggers a recursive or repeated check without consuming the input, it enters a cycle.

## Remediation
To resolve this, ensure that every path through the parsing loop either:
1. Consumes at least one token from the input stream.
2. Explicitly throws an error to break the loop upon encountering an unexpected token sequence.
